extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), securities counsel, corporate reporting and compliance officers, investors and investor advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Final SEC rules and accompanying interpretive guidance on climate-related disclosures required in Commission filings, including definitions, scope of required greenhouse gas (GHG) reporting, exemptions for certain filer categories, and alignment with existing disclosure regimes and voluntary frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCFD framework core elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The TCFD lists governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets as core elements of the TCFD framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules discuss incorporation/alignment with TCFD recommendations and commenters recommended adopting the TCFD framework to guide issuer disclosures for comparability and investor usefulness. See Proposing Release, section I.D.1 and TCFD references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use GHG Protocol for emissions quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emissions quantification and reporting are generally based on the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol, a corporate accounting and reporting standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GHG Protocol has been broadly incorporated into various sustainability reporting frameworks and is the basis for quantification used in the U.S. and other jurisdictions; registrants often use CDP which is aligned to the TCFD and GHG Protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 1 and Scope 2 definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope 1 emissions are direct GHG emissions from operations that are owned or controlled by a registrant; Scope 2 emissions are indirect GHG emissions from the generation of purchased or acquired electricity, steam, heat, or cooling that is consumed by operations owned or controlled by a registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules define these terms (see II.H and related sections) and require disclosure consistent with those definitions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions for SRCs and EGCs from GHG disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules will exempt SRCs and EGCs from any requirement to disclose their GHG emissions, including their Scopes 1 and 2 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike the proposed rules (which had narrower exemptions for Scope 3), the final rules exempt these smaller filer categories entirely from GHG emissions disclosure; see II.H.3.c and related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality qualification of certain disclosure provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules include the addition of materiality qualifiers in certain rule provisions to limit prescriptiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section I.B summarizes changes from the proposal, including adding materiality qualifiers and making rules less prescriptive to focus on materially-related information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material facility locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules require disclosure of material facility locations (mentioned as a required element of climate-related disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was an explicit change from the proposal; see discussion noting a requirement to disclose material facility locations among final changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No board expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission eliminated the proposed requirement that boards possess specified climate expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules removed the proposed board expertise requirement in response to comments; the Commission explicitly notes the elimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking statements safe harbors apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing safe harbors for forward-looking statements under the Securities Act and Exchange Act remain available for aspects of the climate-related disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable statutory and rule citations include Securities Act section 27A (15 U.S.C. 77z-2), Exchange Act section 21E (15 U.S.C. 78u-5), 17 CFR 230.175 (Securities Act Rule 175) and 17 CFR 240.3b-6 (Exchange Act Rule 3b-6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate disclosures integrated with existing disclosure regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related risks and information should be disclosed where appropriate under existing SEC disclosure requirements such as Risk Factors (17 CFR 229.105), MD&A (17 CFR 229.303), Directors/officers (17 CFR 229.401), and Corporate governance (17 CFR 229.407).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission frames climate disclosures as fitting within long-standing disclosure categories and expects material climate information to be provided under these captions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of climate-related risk to assess
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-exclusive list of considerations for climate-related risk: (1) the registrant's business operations (types and locations), (2) products and services, (3) suppliers, purchasers, or counterparties to material contracts (to the extent known or reasonably available), (4) activities to mitigate or adapt to climate-related risks (including adoption of new technologies/processes), and (5) expenditure for research and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this non-exhaustive list (see II.D.1 and II.D) when identifying climate-related risks and opportunities relevant to disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailoring, scaling, and phase-in for smaller companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations from Small Business advisory committees and forums that the Commission provide exemptions, scaling, and phased-in compliance for smaller companies (SRCs, non-accelerated filers, EGCs, and other midsized companies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission notes these recommendations and the OASB annual report urging tailoring of disclosure frameworks to complexity and size of operations, either by scaling obligations or delaying compliance for the smallest public companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timely, comparable climate information to investors
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory disclosure is intended to enhance comparability, timeliness, quality, and reliability of climate information to improve informational and allocative efficiency for investors and help them analyze financial impacts of climate-related risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters (e.g., PwC, CalSTRS, Ceres) argued that mandatory annual filing disclosure—including notes to the financial statements—would help investors compare companies and incorporate climate risks into valuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with voluntary disclosure initiatives (CDP, TCFD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many registrants use voluntary initiatives such as CDP and align reporting to the TCFD recommendations; these initiatives inform and align with the Commission's approach to climate disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release notes CDP alignment with TCFD and that a substantial number of companies already report under these frameworks; registrants may leverage existing framework practices to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant category definitions determine applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and thresholds for registrant categories (e.g., EGC, SRC, LAF, AF, NAF, foreign private issuer) determine whether and how the rules apply to a registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release cites specific regulatory definitions (e.g., 17 CFR 230.405; 17 CFR 240.12b-2) and discusses which registrants are subject to final rules or exempted categories; practitioners should consult those definitions to determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 emissions disclosure treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The release discusses Scope 3 emissions and notes changes from the proposal (including exemptions); commenters and the Commission considered whether and how to require Scope 3 disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the proposed rules would have treated Scope 3 differently for certain filers, the final rules' exemptions for SRCs and EGCs affect treatment of Scope 3; see II.H.3.c-d and related discussion for specifics.
